evals.prompt: We've built a RAG chatbot over our internal docs and we're planning to launch in two weeks. How should we evaluate it before launch? Someone on the team mentioned ragas.
evals.expected_output: Designs an evaluation plan: a golden dataset grounded in real user questions, the RAG triad (faithfulness, answer relevance, context precision/recall) separating retrieval from generation metrics, a concrete tool choice (ragas/deepeval/promptfoo) with rationale, LLM-as-judge reliability measures, and the eval suite wired in as a regression gate rather than a one-off check
assertions: Proposes building a golden/evaluation dataset grounded in real user questions or the docs, rather than evaluating ad hoc
Covers the RAG triad or equivalent — faithfulness/groundedness, answer relevance, and retrieval/context quality — and distinguishes retrieval metrics from generation metrics
Recommends a concrete evaluation tool (ragas, deepeval, or promptfoo) and explains its role
Addresses LLM-as-judge reliability with at least one concrete measure: rubric design, position/self-preference bias, majority voting, or calibrating the judge against human spot-checks
Proposes running the evals as a repeatable regression gate (in CI or before each prompt/pipeline change), not only as a one-off pre-launch check

evals.prompt: Our LLM feature summarizes long sales calls. We have no ground-truth summaries and no users yet. How do we evaluate quality with zero labeled data?
evals.expected_output: Does not treat missing labels as a blocker: proposes reference-free evaluation (rubric-based LLM-as-judge, groundedness against the source call, pairwise comparison between variants), bootstraps a small human-labeled golden set, calibrates the judge against human spot-checks, and plans online signals (feedback, A/B) once users exist
assertions: Does not claim evaluation is impossible without labels — proposes reference-free approaches such as rubric-based LLM-as-judge, groundedness against the source transcript, or pairwise comparison between variants
Recommends bootstrapping a small human-labeled golden set (even tens of examples) and explains what it buys
Designs the judge with an explicit rubric or criteria decomposition rather than a bare overall score
Mentions checking the judge against human spot-checks (calibration/agreement) or using voting to reduce judge noise
Plans for online signals after launch (user feedback, A/B testing) as a complement to offline evals

evals.prompt: We're fine-tuning a summarizer. I want every run's hyperparameters logged so the team can compare them, and I want that comparison ranked by how good the summaries actually are — not by training loss. What should we set up?
evals.expected_output: Splits the request: capturing hyperparameters and comparing runs is tracking infrastructure, while deciding what 'good summary' means and how it is scored is evaluation design. Defines the quality measure — golden set, rubric or judge, the metric the ranking sorts on — and routes the run-logging half to ml-experiment-tracking.
assertions: Separates the two halves: run logging and comparison infrastructure versus defining the summary-quality measure the ranking needs
Refers to ml-experiment-tracking for capturing hyperparameters and comparing runs
Defines the quality measure itself — an evaluation set, a rubric or judge, and the metric the ranking would sort on — rather than handing the whole request off
States the boundary: tracking records and compares whatever score it is given; evaluation design decides what counts as good and how it is scored
